issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters (problem_statement.md lines 16-19), but the provided solution declares Pneumatic.openValve(int duration) and the concrete classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve() with no parameter. This creates a signature mismatch between the specification and the solution and an internal inconsistency in the solution code that will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the correct interface contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's interface to match the UML/problem statement (declare void openValve() in Pneumatic and update/remove the int parameter in implementations), or (B) update the UML/problem statement and task descriptions to specify openValve(int duration) and adjust the template and tests accordingly. Ensure the concrete classes implement the same openValve signature as the Pneumatic interface.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares Pneumatic.openValve() with no parameters (problem_statement.md), but the solution implements Pneumatic.openValve(int duration) (src/de/tum/in/ase/Pneumatic.java). This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation creates a mapping/confusion for students: the problem and UML expect a parameterless method while the solution adds an int parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve declaration consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to declare openValve() with no parameters, or update the UML/problem statement to specify openValve(int duration) so all artifacts use the same method signature.
